newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Sacked Hungary minister denies blame.
newsitem.headline: Sacked Hungary minister denies blame.

text.p: Sacked Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman on Thursday denied any legal responsibility for the scandal which has engulfed Hungary's privatisation agency APV and led to his dismissal.

Suchman was speaking publicly for the first time about the case in which a consultant Marta Tocsik was paid a "success fee" of 804 million forints ($5.2 million) for negotiating compensation deals for APV with local authorities for land on which privatised state companies were located.

"In the Tocsik affair I have no legal responsibility. I gave no orders. I did not condone the affair. I do not know the lady. And I don't have the money," Suchman told Hungarian news agency MTI after appearing before Parliament's Constitutional Committee which is investigating the affair.

Hungary's Chief Prosecutor said on Tuesday he had ordered an investigation of the activities of Tocsik and other unnamed APV officials and on Wednesday the Constitutional Committee began its own inquiry at which Tocsik failed to appear.

Suchman told the Constitutional Committee on Thursday that total claims of local councils against APV amounted to 40 to 80 billion forints ($250 million to $500 million) but the 1996 central budget had allocated only 15 billion forints ($95 million) to the APV this year to satisfy the claims.

Suchman said he accepted political responsibility for the affair but maintained there was no corruption at APV. He said the only issue was Marta Tocsik's unlawful practices and the exorbitant fee she had received for her services.

Asked by the committee whether the government was aware of the bargain with local councils and if so why it did not take a decision on the matter, Suchman said the cabinet and Prime Minister Gyula Horn were aware of the negotiations, but that there was no need for the government to intervene.
Suchman was dismissed by the prime minister on Sunday and will remain in office until October 15.
Horn on Thursday evening promised tough action to stamp out corruption in state-run agencies.
"Society must come together to fight corruption," he told Hungarian Television, adding that anti-corruption agencies will be strengthened.
Horn said the new leadership of the state privatisation agency APV would ensure that there would be no repeat of the so-called "Tocsik scandal".

Horn on Wednesday appointed Judit Csiha as minister in charge of the state privatisation agency APV to replace Suchman and Arpad Kovacs as president of the APV board of directors and Andras Laszlo as APV general manager to replace Imre Szokai and Istvan Kocsis.
"These three will ensure that laws are respected," he said.
